name: C2PA Sign
description: Signs compatible media assets with C2PA Content Credentials (content-provenance manifests) when files are uploaded, when content is published, and when image derivatives are generated, by shelling out to the c2patool binary with a configured certificate/key pair.
project_description: C2PA Sign digitally signs media assets with C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) Content Credentials so their origin and edit history can later be authenticated. It integrates with the jrglasgow/c2patool PHP wrapper library, which in turn drives the contentauth c2patool command-line utility. The module signs media files upon upload (via the file widget/hook_entity_presave on file entities), signs files attached to content entities upon publication (hook_entity_insert/update on nodes and other content entities), and signs image-style derivatives as they are generated (kernel RESPONSE subscriber). Signing requires a configured certificate/private-key pair (a directory of matching .pem/.key files, or the C2PA_SIGN_CERT / C2PA_PRIVATE_KEY environment variables) and a c2patool binary path. Manifests are assembled as PHP arrays (title, claim_generator, actions such as c2pa.created/c2pa.published/c2pa.resized, and custom drupal.c2pa_sign.* assertions), dispatched through alterable events, written to a temp file, and passed to c2patool. Certificate usage is counted per public-key fingerprint in the c2pa_sign_certificate_uses table, and admins are warned when the active certificate is near expiry. Configuration lives at /admin/config/media/c2pa_sign (permission: administer site configuration).
